messages:
sara: heads-up — while testing long session workloads (50k+ tokens) i'm seeing continuous memory growth in the KV cache for a single session. reuse rate reported by kvstat is only ~22% for predicted prefixes. looks like prefix reuse across subsequent requests isn't happening consistently. :thinking:

mike: can you paste the kvstat snippet? are we seeing a lot of unique keys per session or fragmentation due to small variations?

sara: pasted below from a short run (truncated):
```
kvstat --session s:abc123 --window 1h
total_keys: 12456
unique_prefixes: 9810
reuse_hits: 2723 (21.9%)
evictions: 432
avg_prefix_len: 48
largest_fragment: 312MB
```
Noticing many keys with same first 8 tokens but different trailing role/sep tokens.

jordan: hmm. that avg_prefix_len seems high vs typical. Are we hashing the full prefix text including user metadata? If so slight differences will produce distinct keys.

nina: earlier proposal was to make cache key based on a normalized prefix fingerprint (token ids) and drop ephemeral system tokens. Maybe we never landed that normalization in the streaming path.

lee: i dug into the runtime traces — the key derivation in streaming path currently uses `session_id + model + start_token_index + context_marker`. That makes them too granular. It was intended for per-offset caching for partial completions, but for cross-request reuse we should canonicalize by prefix content not start index.

mike: agrees. small experiment: if we collapse key to `model + sha256(prefix_tokens[:N])` where N is up to last user message, reuse jumps. Ran 1k requests to same session with that change: reuse ~71%, mem growth stabilized.

sara: can you share the exact key function you used? need to check collision risk vs fragmentation tradeoff.

mike: yep — quick prototype:
```
# pseudo
prefix_tokens = tokenize(prefix_text)
trimmed = prefix_tokens[-1024:]  # bound to last 1024 tokens
fingerprint = sha256(bytes(trimmed))
cache_key = f"{model}:{fingerprint}"
```
We also remove role/system tokens before hashing. No user-visible collision observed in short run.

jordan: two things: 1) we must keep some session stickiness for interactive editing (where partial caches keyed by index help fast resume). 2) we can have dual-key entries: a canonical prefix key (high reuse) and an offset key (fast short-term resume) with pointers to same KV blocks. That would reduce duplication.

nina: +1 to dual-key. eviction policy: prefer keeping canonical keys long (Larger TTL) and make offset keys ephemeral. That should keep mem footprint bounded.

lee: note: fragmentation also comes from differing quantization binning per worker. If two workers quantize KV blocks differently we can't share them across shards even with same key. We should ensure canonicalization includes quantization profile id. e.g., key = model:quant_profile:prefix_hash.

kv-monitor-bot: [alert] eviction-rate spiked on shard gpu-7 at 2026-10-02T14:12Z — 420 evictions in 10m window. avg reuse 19.8%.

mike: thanks, that matches my perf window. Proposal PR sketch:
- change streaming key derivation to normalized prefix fingerprint (drop role/system tokens)
- add dual-key mapping (canonical prefix -> KV block, offset key -> pointer with short TTL)
- include quant_profile id in key namespace
- add metric: prefix_collision_rate and canonical_reuse_ratio

sara: sounds good. what about rollout plan? A/B by model or by session? Would prefer to limit to a canary fleet first.

jordan: canary by session type: 1) small chat sessions (<2k tokens) 2) long sessions (>=10k tokens). Start with small percentage (5%) of long sessions on canary. Monitor memory growth, reuse, and quality regressions.

mike: i'll open the PR and include perf harness results comparing old vs new keying on long-session replay. Early numbers: old mem per-session growth ~430MB/10k tokens, new ~70MB/10k tokens. reuse +50 p.p.

nina: add an eval to check output parity for ~500 prompts to catch regressions (prefix normalization could change what we serve if system tokens were intentionally included).

lee: i'll add quant_profile to the worker handshake to avoid mismatches and a migration path for existing entries (bg compaction job to populate canonical keys).

sara: assign owners: mike -> PR + perf numbers, lee -> quant_profile compatibility, nina -> eval suite, jordan -> rollout plan + canary gating. i'll own postmortem if things go sideways. :thumbsup:

mike: noted, will have PR by EOD tomorrow.

jordan: timeline wise, if canary looks good for 72h we can expand to 25% and then full. Keeping watch on kv-monitor metrics.

sara: thanks all. TL;DR: change keying to prefix fingerprints, dual-key for offset resumes, include quant profile in namespace, canary rollout.

kv-monitor-bot: [info] created ticket INF-8421: track canonical_reuse_ratio metric and eviction alerts.
